finding.claim: Stored SSRF: the attacker-supplied callbackUrl is saved and later used as the target of a server-side POST with no scheme, host, or IP validation. An attacker can point it at internal services or cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/) and make the server send the payload to them. The response is discarded, so this is mostly blind SSRF.

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-controlled URL from the request body
URL stored unvalidated in the static subscriptions map
notifyAll iterates the stored URLs on the periodic job
client.send() issues the POST to the attacker-chosen URL

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme check, or private/loopback/link-local IP blocking on any path from subscribe to send. No DNS-rebinding protection. The HttpClient default is no redirect following, which does not mitigate a direct internal URL. Note that thumb() at line 30 is not a finding: it has a fully anchored regex allowlist (String.matches) pinned to https://cdn.example.com/img/[a-z0-9]+.png, and redirects are not followed.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated, and src/Jobs.java:21,24 pass it to URI.create and client.send with no scheme/host/IP check; the only regex guard at line 30 covers thumb(), not this path. It is the only source file, so no handler or middleware guard exists, and the endpoint's authentication can't be assessed from this code.
